newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 23.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says the government will not tolerate "illegal acts" after shopkeepers threatened "tax obstructionism" against the 1997 budget (all).
* Majority parties are still seeking an agreement over the proposed tax modifications in the 1997 budget (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi will ask the European Commission in Brussels to examine Italy's 1997 budget (Corriere, Repubblica).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro says an agreement over constitutional reforms must be found soon, otherwise "the country will sink" (all).
*The government is expected to call a vote of confidence in the lower house of Parliament to ensure passage into law of the decree detailing a rescue plan for Banco di Napoli (all).
* October CPI in the second group of sample cities confirm inflation is heading down and analysts now forecast a year on year rate off 3 percent (all).

* Agnelli family holding group IFI had the strongest revenues in 1995, overperforming state industrial holding IRI. It is the first time a private group does better than a public one, and this is seen as a result of privatisations (all).
*Carmaker Fiat sold a controlling stake in fund manager Prime to insurance group Generali for 325 billion lire (all).

* Head of antitrust authority Giuliano Amato says Fido, the new "supercordless" telephone which is being launched by Telecom Italia might be considered as "an abuse of a dominant position" on the market (Corriere, Repubblica).
* Olivetti is suing former director general Renzo Francesconi for 100 billion lire. Francesconi resigned in early September after questioning the accuracy of Olivetti's financial statements (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
